transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-08
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Owen Park (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Nebula CTO), Priya Kumar (Head of ML), Lauren Smith (SRE), Evan Zhou (PM)
Shared: redwood-model-selection-deck.pdf, benchmark-template.xlsx (links shared in chat)

[00:00] Nina Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm nina with redwood inference, i'm the account lead, and with me is owen our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marco Diaz: good, thanks. busy week but excited to talk model selection. we've got a few priorities.
[00:12] Priya Kumar: hi, nina, owen. quick background: nebula runs user-facing assistants for financial analytics and legal summarization. we have multi-region infra in GCP (vertex endpoints today) and are exploring inference options to reduce cost and support longer contexts.
[00:28] Owen Park: got it; thanks. high-level question: what's your target latency for interactive flows vs batch?
[00:33] Lauren Smith: interactive needs <= 800ms for short queries, but longer agent sessions can tolerate 2-4s per turn. overall though we want predictable p95.
[00:42] Evan Zhou: also important many sessions are multi-turn with a 40k token history for customer transcripts we surface, sometimes up to 60k.
[00:50] Nina Patel: perfect, that's helpful. on model side are you looking exclusively at open models or are you considering hosted proprietary APIs as well?
[00:56] Marco Diaz: preference for open models because of licensing and cost control, but we might hybridize for certain tasks if quality is far better.
[01:04] Owen Park: great. for open models we typically recommend variants across the fidelity/latency/cost spectrum. for multilingual and long context we have profiles: high-accuracy (larger fp16/8-bit quantized), cost-optimized (16k context quant + cache), and long-context specialty (model variants with 32k/4k positional support).
[01:28] Priya Kumar: can you call out specific model names? we've been testing some 13B and 70B re-hosted variants, and also evaluated a few LLaMA++ forks.
[01:36] Owen Park: sure examples: Mistral and Llama2 derivatives for cost/accuracy sweet spot, Mistral-40B / OpenLlama-70B variants for higher accuracy, and models like Redwind-Long (internal name) or community long-context models that we've validated for 64k sequences. (note: model names may be off in transcript)
[01:56] Marco Diaz: okay two big questions: 1) hosted vs dedicated how big a latency improvement can we expect if we reserve capacity? 2) data residency and KMS for any PII in transcripts.
[02:08] Nina Patel: on latency: dedicated (reserved GPU pools) gives you predictable throughput and lower p95 because you avoid cold-starts and noisy neighbors typical p95 improvements of 20-40% vs shared hosted for the same model family, depending on instance type and batching. for absolute low-latency we'd pair a smaller lower-quant model in the hot path and fallback to higher-accuracy variants for heavy inference.
[02:30] Owen Park: on KMS/data residency: our Private offering (VPC or on-prem) gives you customer-managed KMS and isolated control plane; Dedicated has encryption at rest with customer KMS integration as an option and audit logs. we can share SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes after this call.
[02:49] Priya Kumar: important for us we have regulators asking for key custody and auditability. can you do HSM?
[02:55] Nina Patel: yes, HSM-backed KMS is supported in Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with cloud KMS and provide audit trails we'll attach the security whitepaper.
[03:04] Evan Zhou: about tool-calling we need the assistant to call internal APIs for portfolio lookups and trigger queued jobs. does Redwood support tool-calling patterns and structured outputs?
[03:12] Owen Park: yes we support function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs. we also have streaming responses and can instrument tracing so you can correlate tokens to external API calls in the Redwood Console.
[03:22] Marco Diaz: any limits on number of tool integrations or secrets management?
[03:26] Owen Park: integrations are flexible; secrets should be passed via your sidecar or using Redwood's secrets store which can be integrated with KMS. we'll include best-practice notes in the follow-up doc.
[03:36] Priya Kumar: model accuracy on finance domain we saw hallucinations in some open models for legislative citations. how do you help mitigate that?
[03:44] Owen Park: two things: first, model selection and few-shot prompting tuned to your domain reduces hallucinations; second, we recommend a verification tier run the model with a retrieval-augmented layer (RAG) pulling from your canonical docs and a reranker. Redwood supports routing requests to a 'verifier' model variant before returning results.
[04:04] Nina Patel: also quality monitoring and evals: we can set up regression alerts tied to your prompt sets so you get alerts when the model degradates vs baseline.
[04:12] Lauren Smith: good. on infra: our SRE is concerned about batch sizes causing latency spikes. how do you manage batching and KV cache?
[04:20] Owen Park: runtime does continuous batching with workload-aware policies and per-customer token limits; KV cache for prefix tokens is supported to avoid re-compute. you can tune batch windows; in Dedicated we expose more fine-grained knobs and we can set SLOs.
[04:34] Marco Diaz: cost what's the unit economics difference between hosted and dedicated roughly?
[04:38] Nina Patel: hosted is usage-based and good for variable traffic; dedicated is monthly committed capacity and you typically see 30-60% cost savings at scale because of reserved GPU utilization. exact numbers depend on model family and inference profile; we'll include scenario pricing in the worksheet.
[04:57] Evan Zhou: timeline: we want to pick a path within 3-4 weeks, pilot in Q1. are you able to support a pilot with 1-2 week benchmarks?
[05:06] Nina Patel: yes; typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. next step would be a benchmark plan (we'll run on your sample prompts and languages) and a trial on Dedicated or Hosted with a small reserved pool.
[05:18] Priya Kumar: languages we need EN, ES, FR, JA, and decent tokenization for long transcripts. any issues with multilingual models at 64k?
[05:27] Owen Park: multilingual long-context is challenging; some model variants support 64k natively, others require sliding window + RAG. our recommendations: a long-context multilingual model for core context and a lightweight local summarizer to compress history into summaries for prompt efficiency. we'll lay out three recommended options in the follow-up: 1) high-accuracy long-context model, 2) hybrid long-context + summarizer, 3) cost-optimized segmented context approach.
[05:50] Marco Diaz: are there any tricky portability issues if we start hosted and then move to Dedicated or Private?
[05:56] Nina Patel: the API and config layer are the same across modes; model pins and rollouts transfer. data plane integrations (VPC endpoints, KMS) will need configuration during migration but we've done this with multiple customers.
[06:08] Evan Zhou: can we run a quick perf baseline now on a small set?
[06:11] Owen Park: we can, but better if we use your exact prompts and sample signals. please share samples (Priya) and we'll create the benchmark job i'll send the test harness.
[06:21] Priya Kumar: i'll upload ~500 prompts and 3 representative long sessions; goal is to measure p50/p95 latency, token cost, and quality (BLEU/ROUGE plus manual checks).
[06:33] Nina Patel: perfect. any contract/procurement constraints? Marco?
[06:36] Marco Diaz: procurement needs terms for data residency, ok with standard MSP contracts but need SLA language for latency. also want to know if we can have a short-term pilot without long-term commit.
[06:48] Nina Patel: yes, pilot without commit is standard; SLA commitments apply for Dedicated with reserved capacity. we'll put pilot terms in the worksheet.
[06:55] Lauren Smith: one last technical are you able to run on our on-prem GPU for Private? we have some air-gapped requirements for certain customers.
[07:03] Owen Park: yes, Private supports on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments; you'll get the private control plane and can manage keys locally. we'll include a summary of Private deployment requirements.
[07:14] Nina Patel: quick recap: we'll send pricing worksheet, security docs, and a benchmark plan. action items: owen drafts benchmark, nina sends pricing, priya shares prompts. any other items?
[07:28] Marco Diaz: also include the model variant recommendations for multilingual long-context and the tradeoffs.
[07:33] Nina Patel: will do. thanks everyone, we'll schedule the deep-dive next tuesday at your availability.
[07:40] Evan Zhou: thanks talk soon.
